title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Saturday 31 October 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. I'm {A}, and it's Saturday the thirty-first of October. Happy Halloween, if that's your thing.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> Halloween, and the cinema world is a little quieter than usual, to be honest. There's one serious story from Spain we have to start with.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. The Seminci film festival in Valladolid has cancelled its closing gala, out of respect for the victims of the rail accident in the province of Toledo. We'll tell you exactly what stays and what goes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then the happier part. Next Friday, the sixth of November, two very different films open in Spain: the new Godzilla, and a dark period thriller from the Basque Country called Sacamantecas.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: After that, a big biopic series about Muhammad Ali, what's streaming on the opera front, and the dates to keep in your diary. Let's get going.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: All of it is in the written edition, with sources and dates, if you want the details.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, Seminci. This is the seventy-first edition of the Valladolid International Film Week, and it was due to end tonight with its closing gala at the Teatro Calderón.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That gala is now cancelled. The festival says it's out of respect and solidarity with the victims, their families and the injured of the rail accident in Toledo province.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that falls inside the three days of official mourning declared by the Spanish government. So it's not only the gala. The television broadcast on La 2 and RTVE Play is off too.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The Seminci Noche activities as well. The red carpet, all of it. |That makes sense.| It's the right call, I think. A party doesn't sit well next to a national tragedy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, what stays. The screenings in Valladolid's cinemas carry on as scheduled. The festival isn't shutting its doors.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the awards still happen, just differently. The winners will be announced this morning, Saturday, at an information event that replaces the ceremony.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We don't have the winners yet, because the list wasn't out when we wrote this. So we'll bring you the awards in the next edition.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One more detail. The closing film, Hombre al agua, by Gael García Bernal, still screens tonight at eight o'clock at the Teatro Calderón.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A thought on the timing. A festival like this builds its whole last day around that evening. Cancelling it means choosing to lose the glamour and keep the cinema.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that's what they did. The films keep screening, the prizes are still announced, and the work of the filmmakers isn't erased. <sigh> It's just done quietly.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For anyone who followed the festival, the list of Espiga prizes will come out as one announcement, without the usual ceremony. That's the whole change.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We also won't speculate about who wins. We'd rather wait for the real list.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For anyone following the awards, the plan is simple: the list comes out this morning, and we'll go through it with you in the next edition.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And before it, there'll be a short summary of the festival and a tribute to the filmmakers and films that won. A quieter way to say goodbye.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We talked about that closing film earlier this week. What's new today is only the format. So, a sober end to a festival that has had a lot of good cinema.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: If you're in Valladolid today, check the cinema times directly. That's the practical advice.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay, lighter now. Next Friday, the sixth of November, Godzilla Minus Zero opens in Spanish cinemas.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Finally. <chuckle> Takashi Yamazaki is back, and he directs and writes it, like the first one. The one that won the Oscar for visual effects, Godzilla Minus One.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. And this one is set in nineteen forty-nine, two years later. Japan is rebuilding, and then Godzilla comes back.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe return from the first film. And there's a new name, Min Tanaka, who plays a biologist.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One listing says it's the first Japanese production shot in the Filmed for IMAX format. So if you can, big screen.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Dates matter here, so let's be careful. In Japan it opens on the third of November, through Toho. In the US it's the sixth, through GKIDS. And Spain is the sixth, too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Though one outlet put the ninth in a subtitle. The body text of that same article says the sixth, and so do the other sources. So we go with the sixth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's also rated R in the US, which is a first for the franchise, apparently. |No way.| Yes. But I'd say that's a detail, not a verdict.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that's the point: we haven't seen it. We're not judging quality. We're telling you it exists, and when.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Fair. <short pause> So, the other one. Sacamantecas. This is the one that interests me more, honestly.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It's by David Pérez Sañudo, and it's set in Álava, in the Basque Country, at the end of the Third Carlist War. Nineteenth century.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Based on real events. Several women are found strangled near Vitoria. And Ángela, played by Patricia López Arnaiz, comes back to the city because one of the victims is her sister.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Antonio de la Torre plays the killer, Juan Díaz de Garayo, the man known as the Sacamantecas.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: What I like is that it's about the society around the crimes, too. Authorities who would rather hide the murders. That's more than a body-count film.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It had a special screening in the Official Section at the San Sebastián festival this year. It runs a hundred and nine minutes. And it's distributed by Buena Vista International.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One local outlet, Gasteiz Hoy, calls it an uncomfortable film. They praise De la Torre for holding back. <breath> That's one review, so take it as one voice.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There's a small mess in the listings, by the way. eCartelera lists Sacamantecas on Prime Video. But the local sources say cinemas on the sixth, and the platform only later.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So: cinemas on the sixth. The streaming date, nobody knows yet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Other titles show up for that Friday too: Los miserables, Runner, Dante, a few more. We haven't verified details for them, so we won't guess.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Check the showtimes. And for the horror fans listening, Sacamantecas is the real-crime dark side. Godzilla is the popcorn side.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me go back to Godzilla for a second, because the setup is neat. The first film was a small, human story with a giant monster on top. Do you think the sequel keeps that?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We can't say, we haven't seen it. What the sources give us is the premise: nineteen forty-nine, a country still rebuilding, a scientist warning that the monster was never fully destroyed.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The listing even mentions a plan with a name, Operation Narukami. We won't say more, no spoilers.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good. <chuckle> I'll just say that if you liked the first one, the new film has your attention already.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Reception is the open question. The US box office forecasts talk about an opening in the mid-twenty-million-dollar range. Those are forecasts, not results.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right, and the first film opened with eleven million in North America, so even the forecast would be more than double. Still just a forecast, though.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And for Sacamantecas, one more thing about the production. It was filmed partly in Vitoria-Gasteiz, in February, and also in Agurain, Elciego and Amurrio. Real Álava locations.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's do a quick practical round for that Friday. Two films, one date, and you may want both.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then my order would be Sacamantecas first, then Godzilla. The thriller is the one that depends on you being in the mood. The monster film is the one you'd go to with friends.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <chuckle> That's very sensible, and very unlike you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I contain multitudes. Also, one warning about Sacamantecas: it deals with violence against women in a period setting, and the people who made it say they tried not to turn it into spectacle.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes, the director has talked about that. The challenge was how to show a killer without making the violence the attraction. Patricia López Arnaiz also says the story still feels current because of gender violence today.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's their reading, and it's a serious one. It's why the film is more than a history lesson.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the title, if you've never heard it: the Sacamantecas is a real nickname from nineteenth-century Álava. It's part of local memory.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is why it's strong stuff for a Spanish audience, and maybe less known abroad.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: With RTVE and the Basque broadcaster EITB involved, according to the sources. A properly local production, but with Disney's distribution behind it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The cast is deep, too. Beyond the two leads, there's Josean Bengoetxea and Eneko Sagardoy, among others.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is the sort of cast that makes a period film feel lived in.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <giggle> Popcorn with an Oscar attached.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now streaming. The Greatest, in Spanish El más grande, arrives on Prime Video on Wednesday the fourth of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's a miniseries about Muhammad Ali, eight episodes. Jaalen Best plays him, Cassius Clay at the start.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Michael B. Jordan is an executive producer, through his company Outlier Society. The showrunner is Ben Watkins.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: What's interesting is the authorisation. According to the sources, it's the first scripted series fully authorised by Ali's estate. His widow, Lonnie Ali, is an executive producer.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And it focuses on the early years, nineteen sixty to nineteen sixty-four. The making of the champion, more than the legend.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's a smart choice. Everyone knows the late story. The early years are where the drama is.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Again, a note of honesty. We haven't watched it. It's a period sports biopic, and its quality depends on how it's done.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: You need a Prime Video subscription. And, in Spain, the fourth of November, according to Público's guide.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Same guide says the second season of Ciudad de Dios, la lucha no para, lands on HBO Max on the eighth of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But another source only says November. So <short pause> treat the eighth as unconfirmed.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The series is, I suppose, a different kind of bet from the films. A long form lets you follow the boxer outside the ring.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that is the stated focus. The transformation of Cassius Clay into Ali, rather than a greatest-hits tour of his fights.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For the record, it's eight episodes, so you can finish it in a couple of weekends.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Whether it's good, we'll know when people have watched it. Come back to the Radar then.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And a reminder of how we handle series on this show. They are tracked separately. They don't go in the list of recommended titles at the end of the edition.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. That list is for films and complete recordings with a verified year.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Our stage section. And I'll be straight with you. Today we have no new complete theatre or opera recording that we can verify enough to recommend.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But the calendar has something. OperaVision lists De Materie, by Louis Andriessen, from Opera Ballet Vlaanderen, on the sixth of November at seven in the evening, Central European Time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a modern piece, a big one. And then Britten's Peter Grimes, from the Finnish National Opera and Ballet, on the twenty-sixth, at six.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: OperaVision says it offers new performances every week for free. But the page doesn't say these two are free, or how long they stay online. So we can't promise.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And we can't say whether De Materie is live or a recording. The new production, by Phia Ménard, played in Antwerp back in September.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No cast, no recording year, no subtitles. So it isn't a recommended complete recording yet. It's a date to watch.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The Liceu, meanwhile, brings I Capuleti e i Montecchi to LiceuOPERA+ on the twenty-second of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Bellini. That one we mentioned earlier this week. It's in the calendar again for a reason: it's a good one to plan around.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's also worth noting what OperaVision is. A European platform, supported by the Creative Europe programme, that streams opera for free according to its own description.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So the practical advice: look at the page on the day, see the availability, and don't assume it stays online.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For a modern piece like De Materie, that's a good reason to make an evening of it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And to be clear, we separate the dates from the recommendation. A date is a fact. A recommendation needs a full recording we can describe, and today we don't have one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Quick calendar. Today, Saturday: Seminci's winners in the morning, no gala, and Hombre al agua at eight tonight.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Tuesday the third: Godzilla Minus Zero opens in Japan. Wednesday the fourth: The Greatest on Prime Video, and the Tokyo festival wraps up.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Friday the sixth in Spain: Godzilla, Sacamantecas, and De Materie on OperaVision.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then Sunday the twenty-second for the Liceu, and Thursday the twenty-sixth for Peter Grimes. Done.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One thing to keep in mind with the dates: the Japan opening on the third is for Japan only. Spain waits until the sixth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Always the territory. We don't guess a Spanish date from a Japanese one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Picks time. First, Sacamantecas. Our editorial affinity is four out of five, with medium confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It fits the taste for period films and dark auteur cinema. A thriller about a society that prefers silence. We haven't seen it, and we've only read one local review, so medium confidence.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Second, Godzilla Minus Zero. Three out of five, low confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Low, because it's early. Reception is thin. It's period monster cinema, and its strength is the scale. Seen on a big screen, it could be wonderful. <chuckle> Or not. We'll see.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And third, The Greatest, also three out of five and low confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Quick reminder that The Greatest is a series, so it's in the picks, but not in the recommended titles list.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. That one is films only.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A sports biopic. It'll depend on the execution. Remember, these are editorial affinity scores, not critics' marks.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Nothing from the opera side today, since we can't verify a recording. But the dates are there.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: If you can only pick one for next weekend, I'd say Sacamantecas, because it's the one with the stronger match to what this Radar looks for.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Agreed, though I'd go to Godzilla for the sound alone. <laugh> Roaring in IMAX, that's the whole point.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Just remember, it's a recommendation based on what we've read, not on what we've seen. We say that every time, and we mean it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: If a review changes our mind, we'll tell you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sacamantecas and Godzilla are also in the list of recommended titles at the end of the edition, if you want to copy it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, the idea of the day. A festival chooses sobriety over spectacle, and a quiet week opens into a Friday with a monster and a murderer.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Take care of each other this weekend. Thanks for listening. See you tomorrow on the Radar.

pronunciations.Ciudad de Dios, la lucha no para: See-oo-dad deh Dee-ohs, lah Loo-chah noh Pah-rah
